config.title: Build structured logging formatters

intro.title: Build structured logging formatters
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a structured logging formatter, a tool that converts log messages into a consistent, machine-readable format like JSON. You'll learn how to create a function that accepts log data and outputs it as a structured object, making logs easier to search and analyze. The core programming concept involves using JavaScript objects and methods to format and serialize data. You'll work with Node.js's built-in console and JSON utilities to implement this formatter, applying key skills in data handling and output formatting.
intro.usecase: Structured logging formatters are essential in production Node.js applications where logs need to be parsed and analyzed by monitoring systems. In e-commerce platforms, structured logs help track user transactions, inventory changes, and API response times in formats that tools like Elasticsearch or Splunk can index. Financial services use structured logging to audit transactions with consistent timestamps, severity levels, and metadata for compliance reporting. This pattern also powers developer dashboards that visualize application performance metrics and error rates from formatted log streams.

objectives: Implement a basic structured logging formatter function in Node.js
Configure log formatters to output JSON-structured messages
Manipulate log data to include timestamps and severity levels
Integrate custom formatters with the console logging methods
Construct a reusable formatter module for consistent log formatting
Apply formatting options to control log output structure
Initialize a logging utility with structured formatting capabilities

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the fs (file system) and path modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import built-in Node.js modules. The fs module provides file system operations, and path helps with file path manipulation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fs and path modules are imported and ready to use for file operations and path handling.
successCriteria: fs and path modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you import both modules: fs for file system operations and path for path handling. Both should use require() statements.
steps.feedbackWrong: import two built-in Node.js modules: fs (file system) and path (path utilities). Use require() statements for both.

steps.title: Create the main logging formatter function
steps.instruction: Create a function named formatLog that takes level, message, and timestamp as parameters. The function should return an object containing these three properties.
steps.hint: Define a function with three parameters. Inside the function, return an object with keys 'level', 'message', and 'timestamp' mapped to the parameter values.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required modules here

// Create the formatLog function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named formatLog is defined that accepts three parameters and returns an object with those values.
successCriteria: The formatLog function is defined with three parameters (level, message, timestamp) and returns an object containing those properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the function, but make sure it takes all three parameters and returns an object with level, message, and timestamp properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The formatLog function isn't properly defined. It should accept three parameters and return an object containing those values.

steps.title: Add basic log formatting logic
steps.instruction: Inside the formatLog function, return a formatted string that combines a timestamp, log level, and message using template literals.
steps.hint: Use backticks (`) to create a template literal that includes the timestamp, level, and message parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The formatLog function should return a properly formatted log string when called with timestamp, level, and message arguments.
successCriteria: formatLog returns a string combining timestamp, level, and message using template literals
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using template literals and returning the formatted string from the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The formatLog function doesn't return a formatted string. Check that you're using template literals and returning the combined timestamp, level, and message.

steps.title: Create a log writer function
steps.instruction: Create a function named writeLog that takes timestamp, level, and message parameters, calls formatLog with those parameters, and logs the result to the console.
steps.hint: Define a new function that accepts the same three parameters as formatLog, calls formatLog inside it, and uses console.log to output the formatted string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A writeLog function is created that will format and output log messages when called.
successCriteria: The writeLog function is defined, accepts three parameters, calls formatLog, and logs the result with console.log.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the writeLog function, but it needs to accept parameters, call formatLog, and log the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The writeLog function isn't properly defined yet. Make sure it accepts parameters, calls formatLog, and logs the result.

steps.title: Add structured JSON formatting
steps.instruction: Create a function named formatJsonLog that takes timestamp, level, and message parameters and returns a JSON stringified log object.
steps.hint: Define a function that creates an object with the parameters and uses JSON.stringify to convert it to a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A formatJsonLog function that returns JSON stringified log objects.
successCriteria: The formatJsonLog function is defined, takes three parameters, creates an object with them, and returns JSON.stringify(logObject).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes three parameters and returns a JSON stringified object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you're creating an object with the parameters and using JSON.stringify.

steps.title: Implement file logging capability
steps.instruction: Create a function named writeLogToFile that takes a formatted log string and writes it to a file using fs.appendFileSync.
steps.hint: Use the fs module's appendFileSync method to write the log string to a file named 'app.log'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A writeLogToFile function that writes formatted logs to a file.
successCriteria: The writeLogToFile function is defined and uses fs.appendFileSync to write to 'app.log'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function uses fs.appendFileSync and writes to 'app.log'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't use fs.appendFileSync correctly.

steps.title: Create log level validation
steps.instruction: Inside the formatLog function, add validation at the beginning to check if the provided level is one of the allowed log levels: 'info', 'warn', 'error', or 'debug'. If it's not valid, throw an Error with a descriptive message.
steps.hint: Define an array of allowed levels, then use includes() to check if the provided level is in that array. If not, throw new Error('Invalid log level: ...').
steps.expectedOutcome: The formatLog function will now validate the log level parameter before proceeding with formatting.
successCriteria: formatLog includes validation that checks against allowed levels and throws an error for invalid levels
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your validation checks all four allowed levels and throws an error when invalid.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if the level is one of 'info', 'warn', 'error', or 'debug' and throw an error if not.

steps.title: Add timestamp formatting helper
steps.instruction: Create a function named formatTimestamp that returns a timestamp string in ISO format (like '2023-10-05T14:30:00.000Z').
steps.hint: You can use JavaScript's Date object to get the current time and convert it to an ISO string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A formatTimestamp function is added that returns ISO string timestamps.
successCriteria: The formatTimestamp function exists and returns a string in ISO format.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it returns an ISO string timestamp (use .toISOString()).
steps.feedbackWrong: The formatTimestamp function is missing or doesn't return ISO format timestamps.

steps.title: Create main execution function
steps.instruction: Create a function named main that demonstrates all your logging formatters by calling them with sample data.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls formatLog, formatJsonLog, writeLog, writeLogToFile, and formatTimestamp with example arguments.
steps.expectedOutcome: A main function is defined that will serve as the entry point to demonstrate all logging formatters.
successCriteria: A function named main is created that calls at least three of the existing logging functions with sample arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named 'main' and calls multiple logging functions with sample data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main function is missing or doesn't call the logging formatters. Create a function named main that demonstrates all formatters.

steps.title: Execute the logging demonstration
steps.instruction: At the end of your file, call the main function to execute the logging demonstration.
steps.hint: Simply write the function name followed by parentheses to call it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function will execute, demonstrating all logging formatters and producing output in your console.
successCriteria: The main function is called at the end of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've called the main function at the end of the file.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main function hasn't been called yet. Add a call to main() at the end of your file.
